When SpaceX isn't catching rockets, it's signing deals with AI companies. In February, the company behind Starlink acquired xAI, which includes Twitter (now renamed X). SpaceX reached an agreement with Cursor in April, a competitor to Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex. As of August 14, the acquisition has been completed. SpaceXAI (its new name) recently launched the Grok Bot and Grok 4.6 model with Cursor's help.

Updated August 14, 2026: SpaceXAI has completed its acquisition of Cursor.

Updated June 16, 2026: SpaceX acquired Cursor one week after becoming a publicly listed company.

Below is the original updated version:

SpaceX strikes $10 billion deal with Cursor ahead of $60 billion acquisition

Cursor is popular among software engineers who use Macs to write AI code. It was one of the first services to connect large language model AI to the application development process.

In April, SpaceX and Cursor said the two companies were "working closely together to create the world's best programming and knowledge work AI."

The original partnership included SpaceX paying Cursor $1 billion:

Cursor further revealed partnership details the day of its April acquisition:

Cursor is partnering with SpaceX to accelerate our model training efforts. Just six months ago, we launched Composer as our first agentic coding model. Since then, Composer 1.5 scaled reinforcement learning by more than 20x. Composer 2 added continued pre-training to achieve frontier-level performance at a fraction of the cost of other models. Each step up in compute translates into significant gains in model capability. We have always wanted to push our training work further, but have been constrained by compute bottlenecks. Through this partnership, our team will leverage xAI's Colossus infrastructure to significantly advance the intelligence of our models.

SpaceX's partnership with Cursor strengthens a competitor to Anthropic's Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex agentic coding software.
